## 3. Runtime and constraints

Compiled by `pyc.py` for `py_core`; only this subset is allowed (anything else is rejected at compile time):

```text
ints, True/False/None, names, + - & | ^ << >> ~ unary -, not/and/or
  in conditions, one comparison per expression (< <= > >= == !=),
  mem32[addr] loads/stores (also mem32[a] op= v), name op= expr,
  if/elif/else, while/break/continue, pass, global, import (ignored).
  "from <name> import *" where <name>.py sits next to the source file
  inlines that file there (once), so firmware can be split into modules
  that share one global namespace; errors name the original file / line.
  Without such a file, "from <name> import *" reads the SystemVerilog
  package <name>.sv found next to the source or in a -I directory (the
  memory map packages, e.g. video_processor_map_pkg.sv): its
  "localparam ... NAME = expr;" lines become UPPER_CASE constants NAME
  (folded), "import <pkg>::*;" loads that package first, <pkg>::NAME and
  SV literals (32'h0001_0000, 'h40, 16'd10) are understood, so the
  firmware takes its addresses from the same file as the RTL decoders.
  UPPER_CASE module-level names bound once to a constant expression
  (or const(expr)) are folded at compile time.
  def f(a, b): ... return x   functions with positional parameters,
  called as f(x, y) in expressions or statements; recursion is allowed
  up to the core's call depth. Missing return -> None.
  A function passed to irq_handler() is an interrupt handler instead:
  no parameters, no return value, cannot be called directly.
Builtins: irq_handler(fn), irq_enable(), irq_disable(), wait_irq(), halt(value).
  wait_irq() (WAIT_IRQ, 0x3E) stops the core until its interrupt input is high (an enabled
  source pending at the intc), whether interrupts are enabled or not; with them disabled the
  code after it runs first (the race-free sleep: disable, test, wait_irq, enable).
Strings: a string literal (in any expression, e.g. puts("text")) is a
  small int handle; the text goes to a string table in flash at
  STR_BASE (0x8000), outside the boot image, for the firmware to read at
  run time through the flash controller. The table has 512 slots of 64
  bytes (0x8000-0xFFFF): [0] length (0..62), [1] 1 if the string
  continues in the next slot, [2..] the bytes. A handle is the first slot
  number; slots 128..255 are emitted as h - 256 so they fit LOAD_SMALL,
  slots 256..511 as h (a constant). Firmware decodes a handle with
  slot = h if h >= 256 else h & 255.
  strings("a", "b", ...) returns the handle of a block of consecutive
  one-slot strings (each <= 62 bytes), so handle + i selects entry i (a
  block never straddles slot 256, so the decoding holds for handle + i).
  Identical strings share slots.
Not in the hardware fast path (rejected): * / % ** on variables (py_core v1),
** always, default/keyword arguments, closures, lists, dicts, floats, classes.
--core 2 (py_core v2): * // % on variables (BINARY_MUL 0x17, BINARY_FLOORDIV
  0x1E, BINARY_MOD 0x1F: Python's floor division and modulo, a zero
  divisor traps), 256 globals and 32 locals per function.
```

- Register addresses come from the SystemVerilog map packages (`from <pkg> import *`), never hard-coded numbers, so firmware and RTL decoders share one source.
- Every hardware wait has a bound (poll count) and reports a timeout instead of hanging.

## 5. Requirements traceability

- Every register access must match the register map of the block it addresses (its `<ip>/docs/<ip>_prompt.md` section 5/6 and `src/include/<ip>_regs.json`): offset, access type (RO / RW / W1C / CMD), bit fields and reset values.
- Behaviour described below and not covered by a requirement is reported in the review.

## 6. Function

Implement exactly this behaviour (from the reference program's documentation):

```text
video_processor firmware, part 1: py_soc CPU initialisation (library).

Imported by video_proc.py (the program; pyc.py inlines this file at its
"from video_init import *"). Everything here concerns the control CPU only:

  - the py_soc address map and peripheral register offsets;
  - text output on UART 0: putc, puts / say (strings from the flash string
    table, read through the flash controller), dec, hex32, result (one
    [PASS] / [FAIL] line, counted in passes / errors), heading; with the
    GPIO0[28] direct-transcript strap the text goes instead to the GPIO1
    transcript port (one write per character, no UART wait: the testbench
    writes it straight to the transcript file) and only the tracking
    sections are written (con: 0 muted, 1 UART 0, 2 transcript port);
  - cpu_isr(pending): the CPU's own interrupt sources (software interrupt,
    GPIO2 edge, watchdog pre-timeout, timer, the wake sources), called by
    the program's handler;
  - waiting without polling: wait_bit / port_wait / rx_word / pause sleep
    on the peripheral's interrupt (py_core WAIT_IRQ, interrupts disabled
    around the test so none is missed), every sleep bounded by the SYSCTL
    timer compare interrupt (TMO);
  - cpu_init(start): report section 1 (boot-up sequence: reset cause, the
    boot image header read back from flash, boot status, SoC ID, start-up
    cycle count) and section 2 (peripheral self-test, one PASS / FAIL line
    each: system control, interrupt controller, GPIO loopback and edge
    interrupt, UART 1 / UART 0 loopback, SPI 0 / SPI 1 loopback, I2C 0
    camera control registers, I2C 1 EEPROM, SPI flash, watchdog);
  - section 3 (CPU register dump): every CPU peripheral register with a
    short description (skipped when the GPIO0[31] quick-simulation strap is
    high);
  - the last step of cpu_init: after a successful boot (every self-test
    passed) the core logic reset is released by writing SYSCTL CORE_RESET;
    the logic outside the CPU (the video datapath) is held in reset until
    then, and stays there when a self-test failed;
  - dump(), reg_line(), dump_port(): register dump helpers.

The interrupt handler must be installed (irq_handler) before cpu_init: the
self-test waits for interrupts.
```

Per function:

```text
direct: 1 with the GPIO0[28] direct-transcript strap (only the tracking is written).

putw: Up to 4 characters packed in w, the first in [7:0], ended by a 0 byte: text printed without
reading the flash string table (the per-frame tracking lines; a flash read is several us).

flash_read: Start a READ (03h) of n bytes at addr; the bytes arrive on the flash data port. 0 when the
controller stays busy (timeout), else 1.

flash_byte: Next byte of a flash read (0 after a timeout: the read never delivers it).

str_addr: Flash address of string handle h's first slot (pyc string table: 64-byte slots, length,
continue flag, text).

str_len: Length of string handle h's first slot (0: empty string).

puts: Print string handle h.

hexs: Hex digits of v from bit position top (28: 8 digits, 8: 3 digits) down to 0.

result: One self-test line: [PASS] or [FAIL] and the description; counts the outcome.

deadline: CYCLES + n (mod 2**32): the end of a wait of n cycles (n < 2**31).

passed: True once CYCLES has reached t (wrap-safe).

sleep_until: Interrupts disabled: sleep until an interrupt comes, at the latest when CYCLES reaches t (the
timer interrupt; the handler turns it off), let the handler run, then disable them again.

pause: Sleep n cycles (other interrupts are served meanwhile).

wait_bit: Sleep until mem32[addr] & mask is non-zero (want 1) or zero (want 0); src: the intc source
whose interrupt says so, enabled while waiting (the handler masks it again when it comes). 1, or
0 when TMO cycles pass first. A leaf (deadline, passed and sleep_until written out): it is called
from deep in the text output and py_core has 16 call frames, one kept for the handler.

port_src: intc source of a peripheral's data port (I2C: shared with its done interrupt).

port_wait: Sleep until the data port's PSTATUS bit is set, on its interrupt (IRQ_EN en); 1, or 0 on timeout.

rx_word: Next word from a data port's RX FIFO (sleeping until one arrives), or -1 after a timeout.

wreg: Write v to the register at addr. While log_wr is set (set-up phases) the write is reported on
UART 0: h is a strings() block of three entries, "<module> <register>" and two lines saying what
the change does (the second may be ""), printed as
    <module> <register>
      old value 0x........
      new value 0x........   (read back after the write)
      <what the change does>

dump: n registers from base; names is a strings() block, one padded name + description each.

dump_port: Data port: STATUS and IRQ_EN (TXDATA is write only, reading RXDATA would pop the FIFO).

cpu_isr: The CPU's own interrupt sources; pending = INTC MASKED.

uart_drain: Sleep until UART 0 has sent everything and the echo of it is back: the data port's TX FIFO empty
(interrupt), then the UART's own FIFO (2 words) and shift register (4 character times), then its TX and
RX engines idle (STATUS [1:0]; the UART has no interrupt for that).

cpu_init: Report sections 1-3 (boot-up, self-test, CPU register dump); start = CYCLES when the program
started. Leaves the CPU's interrupt sources enabled and interrupts on (the handler must already
be installed). Nothing outside the CPU is touched; at the end, if every self-test passed, the
core logic reset is released (SYSCTL CORE_RESET). Returns 1 when the core logic is running.
```

## 6a. Industry reference check

Comparison of section 6 with published engineering references. Every difference is a `TODO(REF-...)` written as a prompt for updating the program.

```text
// Industry reference check - video_init.py (2026-10-16)
// Sources:
//   [1] ip/cpu/py_core/tools/pyc.py header (supported Python subset) and
//   ip/cpu/py_core/docs/py_core_prompt.md
//   [2] Register maps of the addressed blocks: <ip>/src/include/<ip>_regs.json and section 5/6
//   of <ip>/docs/<ip>_prompt.md (video_pipeline, vision_system, blur_sharpen, frame_counter,
//   object_tracker, feature_detect, symbol_overlay, py_soc peripherals)
//   [3] Texas Instruments, "TL16C550C Asynchronous Communications Element", SLLS177H (2006),
//   https://www.ti.com/product/TL16C550C - baud = f_clk / (16 x divisor), mid-bit sampling
//   [4] NXP, "I2C-bus specification and user manual", UM10204 Rev. 7.0 (2021),
//   https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/user-guide/UM10204.pdf - 3.1 (START / STOP, ACK, arbitration,
//   clock stretching), Table 10 (tLOW / tHIGH)
//   [5] Winbond, "W25Q128JV 3V 128M-bit Serial Flash Memory" datasheet Rev. M (2024),
//   https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/7161/256_W25Q128JV.pdf - 8.1
//   instruction set (9Fh, 03h, 0Bh, 06h, 02h, 20h, D8h, C7h, 05h), SPI modes 0 and 3
// Published algorithm / rules:
//   Firmware rules: the pyc.py subset; register offsets, access types and bit fields as in the
//   blocks' register maps. Drivers: UART (16550-style status / data ports), I2C master
//   transfers (address, length, START, poll DONE / NACK per UM10204 semantics), SPI flash READ
//   03h (W25Q128JV).
// Comparison with this program (section 6):
//   Matches: I2C transfers write ADDR / LEN, clear STATUS, then CTRL = EN | START | READ (START
//   is a command bit, consistent with i2c_master's CMD-type CTRL), poll DONE with a bound,
//   check NACK; flash reads use 03h with a 3-byte address. Differs: flash_read waits for F_BUSY
//   in an unbounded loop (every other wait uses the bounded wait_set / wait_clear).
// RESOLVED(REF-VIDEO_INIT-1) [LOW] Bounded flash wait. Resolution: 2026-10-16: flash_read uses
//   wait_clear and returns 0 on a timeout; flash_byte is bounded by TMO.
```
